answer_1.quote: this paper focuses on the task of citing sentence generation, which entails identifying salient information from cited papers and capturing connections between cited and citing papers.
answer_1.outputs: citing sentences that describe a cited paper in the context of a citing paper

answer_2.quote: Following previous work, we report ROUGE-1 (unigram), ROUGE-2 (bigram), and ROUGE-L (longest common subsequence) scores to evaluate the generated citing sentences.

answer_4.quote: Three graduate students who are fluent in English and familiar with NLP were asked to rate citing sentences produced by BACO and the re-implemented PTGEN-Cross with respect to four aspects on a 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent) point scale: fluency (whether a citing sentence is fluent), relevance (whether a citing sentence is relevant to the cited paper's abstract), coherence (whether a citing sentence is coherent within its context), and overall quality.
answer_4.guideline: rate citing sentences produced by BACO and the re-implemented PTGEN-Cross with respect to four aspects on a 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent) point scale: fluency, relevance, coherence, and overall quality.
